articles.title: ‘She’s Broke Now. She Just Doesn’t Know It’: Grant Cardone Says a SpaceX Employee Who Just Became a Millionaire and Sold Stock Is Making a Mistake
articles.summary: Grant Cardone isn't impressed by the thousands of people who became millionaires from the SpaceX IPO. Instead, he thinks people should do this instead.
articles.body:
SpaceX's (SPCX) June stock market debut was the most envied payday of 2026. Shares were priced at $135, and an analysis by the investment platform Hill.com, reported by Fortune and The New York Times, estimated that more than 4,000 current and former employees became millionaires on paper. Grant Cardone, in a clip posted to his YouTube channel in September, looked at one of those new millionaires and delivered a verdict: "She's broke. She's broke now. She just doesn't know it."

The employee is hypothetical. Cardone calls her Helen. "Let's just take Helen that works at SpaceX that got a million dollars yesterday, okay?" he said. "If she sells her stock, but she can't, by the way, but if she did, she'd sell her stock, she'd pay $400,000 in taxes, she has 600 grand left," and, as he put it, "she has 600 grand left to live on for 30 years." The interview appears to have been recorded during IPO week in June, when Cardone said Elon Musk had minted "4,800 millionaires" in a matter of days, a figure that is his own and runs a little higher than the published estimate.

Sponsored Content: A $9 Trillion Flying Car Market Is Taking Shape. This Company Is Open to Investors.

Six hundred thousand dollars spread over 30 years is $20,000 a year, which is below the federal poverty guideline for a two-person household, set at $21,150 for 2025 by the Department of Health and Human Services. That is the number that makes "she's broke" land. Everything feeding it, though, rests on Cardone's assumptions: the $400,000 tax bill, the 30-year horizon with no other income, and a lump sum left sitting in cash. The top federal rate of 37% plus a state levy could approach his figure for a high earner in a high-tax state, but an employee holding shares long enough for capital gains treatment would owe considerably less. His aside that she "can't" sell yet refers to the lock-up restrictions that typically bar insider sales for months after a listing.

The verdict serves a rule Cardone has repeated for years: "I only live extravagantly from free cash flow. The only time I spend money is when it's passive income. I never spend any of my earned income, ever," he said. "And I believe this, this is financial advice right here. Okay? Like if a person only spent their passive income, only passive, they would never ever be broke." It is the same thinking behind his long-running advice to the middle class to stop saving and start buying assets that pay, which isn't new.

articles.title: Why Verizon (VZ) Shares Are Trading Lower Today
articles.summary: Shares of telecommunications giant Verizon (NYSE:VZ) fell 6% in the pre-market session after SpaceX agreed to acquire private equity firm Grain Management’s...
articles.body:
Shares of telecommunications giant Verizon (NYSE:VZ) fell 6% in the pre-market session after SpaceX agreed to acquire private equity firm Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, stoking investor concerns over emerging satellite-to-cellular competition.

Grain Management said in a press release that the transaction encompasses 100% of its nationwide 800 MHz holdings, supplying up to 14 MHz of paired low-band airwaves pending Federal Communications Commission clearance.

Writing on X, SpaceX Chief Executive Elon Musk called the agreement a very big deal that secures the spectrum required to achieve complete phone coverage across the United States without requiring specialized handsets.

In research covered by TipRanks, TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge characterized the transaction as a warning to legacy carriers that intensifies pressure to negotiate roaming partnerships.In comments carried by Reuters, William Blair analysts also noted that established operators remain vocal skeptics of whether orbital networks can match terrestrial quality.

Verizon trades on stable postpaid subscriber additions, average revenue per account growth, and the cash generation needed to service substantial debt and protect its dividend yield. Even though 14 MHz of low-band spectrum lacks the throughput to replace urban cell grids, the prospect of a nationwide direct-to-device alternative limits the multiple investors will pay for legacy cellular franchises.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Is now the time to buy Verizon? Access our full analysis report here, it's free .

Verizon's shares are not very volatile and have only had 3 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 3 months ago when the stock dropped 5.3% on the news that it was officially removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average. VZ was replaced by Alphabet ending a decades-long membership.

Also, in a regulatory filing, Verizon disclosed an estimated $700–800 million second-quarter loss from reclassifying assets as held-for-sale in its new 50/50 international joint venture with BT Group, plus $350–450 million in severance and $200–300 million in asset-rationalization charges.Lastly, the overhang from SpaceX's Starlink direct-to-cell ambitions continued to weigh on the long-term competitive story. It is worth noting that the JV loss is a non-cash accounting reclassification tied to strategic streamlining, not a deterioration in the core business. Verizon recently raised FY2026 EPS guidance to roughly $4.95–4.99, beat in Q1, and yields ~6%. Analysts' median target sits near $50, above the session price.

articles.title: Tarifaço dos EUA: quando os efeitos podem chegar ao seu bolso? | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo do Fed de Nova York mostra que as tarifas elevaram a inflação nos EUA. No Brasil, indústrias já enfrentam perda de mercado e pressão sobre o emprego. Para o brasileiro, o impacto nos preços não é automático e pode ocorrer indiretamente, por meio da alta do dólar.
articles.summary: Calçados e máquinas já enfrentam perda de mercado, revisão de contratos e pressão sobre vagas. Para o consumidor, impacto nos preços não é automático e pode aparecer indiretamente.
articles.body:
Um funcionário inspeciona um sapato em uma linha de produção da fabricante brasileira de calçados Kissol, em meio à imposição de novas tarifas americanas sobre diversos produtos brasileiros, incluindo a indústria calçadista, que tem os EUA como seu principal mercado externo. — Foto: Joel Silva/Reuters

Apresentadas pelo governo de Donald Trump como uma forma de proteger a indústria americana, as tarifas impostas pelos Estados Unidos a diversos países também tiveram um efeito contrário ao pretendido: encareceram os produtos para os consumidores do país.

Até fevereiro de 2026, as tarifas acrescentaram 2,9 pontos percentuais à inflação dos produtos comprados pelos americanos, segundo estudo do Federal Reserve de Nova York divulgado nesta semana.

O levantamento também estimou que a tarifa global de 10% sobre todos os produtos importados , anunciada em fevereiro deste ano, elevaria os preços ao consumidor em 2,6% em um período de um ano.

No Brasil, as medidas comerciais anunciadas pelo governo Trump em julho estabeleceram sobretaxas de 12,5% a 25% para diferentes grupos de produtos.

Segundo o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC), as duas medidas alcançam, juntas, 23,1% das exportações brasileiras para os EUA . Desse total, 16,5% estão sujeitos à sobretaxa acumulada de 37,5% . O impacto, porém, varia bastante de acordo com o setor.

🤔 Mas o que isso significa para o cidadão brasileiro? Economistas e representantes do setor afirmam que, no curto prazo, o principal efeito não deve aparecer na etiqueta dos produtos, mas na atividade das empresas e no emprego.

Calçados: setor teme impacto sobre o emprego

O setor calçadista está entre os mais expostos às novas tarifas americanas. Os EUA são um dos principais destinos dos calçados brasileiros, e as exportações já vinham recuando antes mesmo da entrada em vigor das novas medidas.

Entre janeiro e agosto, o Brasil exportou 62,45 milhões de pares de calçados, que renderam US$ 541,45 milhões. Na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025, houve queda de 7,5% no volume e de 16,8% na receita.

Segundo a Abicalçados, são os piores resultados para o período desde 2020, ano fortemente afetado pela pandemia. Apenas em agosto, foram embarcados 7,13 milhões de pares, por US$ 70,8 milhões, quedas de 6,6% e 8,1%, respectivamente.

Os EUA concentram parte importante dessa deterioração. Nos oito primeiros meses do ano, o Brasil exportou 7,38 milhões de pares para o mercado americano , por US$ 120,5 milhões. O volume caiu 4,1% e a receita recuou 22,8% ante o mesmo período de 2025.

A queda da receita foi maior que a do volume. Em agosto, o preço médio do calçado exportado aos EUA caiu 35,4%, para US$ 17,20, segundo a Abicalçados.

A entidade atribui o movimento, entre outros fatores, à mudança no perfil dos produtos vendidos ao mercado americano e à retração das categorias de maior valor, especialmente calçados de couro.

A pressão não vem apenas dos EUA. A Argentina, segundo principal destino dos calçados brasileiros, também reduziu as compras. No acumulado até agosto, as exportações brasileiras para o país caíram 51,6% em volume e 55,6% em receita.

Diante desse cenário, a Abicalçados estima agora uma queda de 7,1% nas exportações brasileiras de calçados em 2026, ante previsão anterior de retração de 3,6%.

Ao mesmo tempo, as importações de calçados avançam no mercado brasileiro. Entre janeiro e agosto, entraram no país 33 milhões de pares , alta de 9,6% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025.

O valor das importações cresceu 11%, para US$ 429,7 milhões. China, Vietnã e Indonésia responderam por cerca de oito em cada 10 pares importados.

O movimento dificulta uma das alternativas para as empresas afetadas pelo tarifaço: vender no Brasil os produtos que deixarem de ser destinados aos EUA.

Haroldo Ferreira, presidente-executivo da Abicalçados — Foto: Divulgação

Segundo Haroldo Ferreira, presidente-executivo da Abicalçados, a indústria enfrenta uma espécie de “efeito pinça”: de um lado, a perda do mercado americano; de outro, a concorrência dos produtos importados no mercado doméstico.

“As empresas poderiam direcionar parte da produção para o mercado nacional para evitar demissões. Mas, com o avanço das importações, fica mais difícil absorver esses produtos e manter os postos de trabalho.”

A entidade estima a perda de mais de 5 mil empregos diretos no segundo semestre caso as tarifas americanas sejam mantidas. Essa é, porém, uma projeção da Abicalçados, e não um número de demissões já registrado.

Os dados mais recentes da própria entidade mostram que, até julho, o setor ainda acumulava saldo positivo de 1.740 postos de trabalho no ano, embora tenha registrado saldo negativo de 387 vagas apenas naquele mês.

Rafarillo: um exemplo de como a tarifa chega à fábrica

Produção de calçados na fábrica da Rafarillo, em Franca (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Facebook

A Rafarillo, fabricante de calçados de Franca (SP), é um exemplo de como a mudança pode afetar a operação de uma empresa. Segundo André Ferreira, representante de comércio exterior da companhia, contratos com compradores americanos precisaram ser renegociados depois do anúncio das tarifas.

A empresa também reorganizou linhas de produção e buscou fornecedores alternativos para reduzir custos.

“O processo produtivo teve que ser repensado, nós tivemos que fazer algumas adequações, de repente até algumas mudanças em relação à matéria-prima, obviamente não mudando a qualidade do produto, mas buscando mais alternativas no mercado", afirmou.

Pedidos menores também passaram a ser negociados. A companhia, que atualmente tem cerca de 150 funcionários, reduziu postos de trabalho e procura novos mercados para compensar parte da perda de vendas aos EUA.

A empresa também tenta ampliar as vendas para outros destinos, incluindo América Latina, Europa, África e Ásia.

Açúcar e etanol: impacto depende do produto

Plantação de cana-de-açúcar — Foto: GATec

No setor sucroenergético, os efeitos são diferentes dos observados na indústria calçadista. O açúcar brasileiro está entre os produtos sujeitos à sobretaxa adicional de 25% prevista na medida específica para o Brasil. Já o etanol está no centro de uma disputa comercial mais ampla entre os dois países.

A União da Indústria de Cana-de-Açúcar e Bioenergia (Unica) afirma que a política brasileira para biocombustíveis é aplicada de forma não discriminatória e segue as regras da Organização Mundial do Comércio ( OMC ).

A entidade também contesta a avaliação americana de que o Brasil deveria oferecer tratamento tarifário preferencial ao etanol produzido nos EUA. Para o açúcar, a relação comercial já era marcada por restrições de acesso ao mercado americano, incluindo cotas tarifárias . Assim, o novo cenário se soma a barreiras que já existiam.

Para o consumidor brasileiro, entretanto, não há uma relação automática entre as novas tarifas e o preço do açúcar ou do etanol. Se ficar mais difícil vender determinado volume aos EUA, produtores podem procurar outros mercados. Parte da produção também pode ser direcionada ao mercado brasileiro.

Em tese, uma oferta maior no mercado interno pode pressionar os preços para baixo ou limitar altas. Mas isso depende de vários fatores, como o volume redirecionado, os preços internacionais, o câmbio e as condições de oferta e demanda.

Por outro lado, se as exportações caírem de maneira significativa, usinas e produtores podem reduzir receitas e investimentos. O efeito pode se espalhar para transportadoras, fornecedores e outros elos da cadeia.

Máquinas: tarifa se soma a um mercado interno enfraquecido

A indústria de máquinas e equipamentos enfrenta pressão tanto no mercado externo quanto no doméstico. Os EUA estão entre os principais destinos das exportações brasileiras, enquanto o mercado interno sofre com juros elevados e baixo nível de investimentos.

No primeiro semestre, o faturamento do setor caiu 13,6% e as vendas no mercado interno recuaram 17%, segundo a Abimaq. As exportações, por outro lado, cresceram 12,7% no período.

Para José Velloso, presidente-executivo da Abimaq, a fraqueza do mercado interno é hoje o principal fator por trás das demissões no setor , com impacto maior do que o tarifaço sobre as empresas exportadoras.

O setor enfrenta um cenário de poucos investimentos no país e menor demanda por máquinas e equipamentos. Segundo Velloso, o faturamento acumula queda de cerca de 17% nos últimos quatro anos, apesar do crescimento das exportações.

Alguns segmentos ligados principalmente ao mercado doméstico enfrentam retrações ainda mais fortes. Segundo Velloso, o faturamento de máquinas agrícolas caiu 25%, enquanto o de colheitadeiras recuou 40%. O cenário, afirma, já levou ao fechamento de fábricas.

“Nós temos uma crise muito importante aqui dentro. Nós temos um aumento das exportações, e isso ameniza, mas temos uma queda das exportações para os Estados Unidos", afirma.

"Essa queda é menor do que o crescimento das exportações que estamos tendo no geral. Então, a tarifa causa demissão? Causa. Mas, quando olho o total do setor, ele está tendo demissões também por causa do baixo desempenho do mercado interno, e não só por causa do tarifaço.”

O efeito pode chegar a empresas que não exportam

Segundo a Abimaq, os EUA compraram cerca de US$ 3,2 bilhões em máquinas e equipamentos brasileiros em 2025.

🔍 O impacto do tarifaço, porém, pode se espalhar pela cadeia produtiva. Uma fabricante que perde pedidos de um comprador americano pode reduzir a produção e, com isso, comprar menos aço, componentes e serviços de fornecedores nacionais, além de reduzir gastos com transporte.

É o chamado efeito em cadeia . Assim, até empresas que nunca exportaram diretamente para os EUA podem sentir os efeitos da queda nas vendas de seus clientes.

A Abimaq afirma ainda que a integração entre as cadeias produtivas brasileira e americana pode fazer com que o aumento de custos atinja empresas dos dois países.

Há, porém, uma dificuldade para medir o impacto sobre o emprego. Segundo Velloso, os dados não permitem separar as demissões provocadas especificamente pelo tarifaço daquelas decorrentes da fraqueza do mercado interno.

Por isso, eventuais cortes de postos de trabalho não poderão ser automaticamente atribuídos às tarifas americanas.

Para o consumidor, o efeito não é uma alta automática de preços

Mas, afinal, o brasileiro pode pagar mais caro por causa do tarifaço?

Não necessariamente. A tarifa é cobrada sobre a entrada do produto nos EUA. Portanto, o primeiro impacto recai sobre a relação comercial entre o exportador brasileiro e o comprador americano.

O mecanismo pode funcionar de diferentes maneiras:

Para manter contratos, exportadores brasileiros podem aceitar preços menores e absorver parte do custo adicional. Isso reduz a margem das empresas, mas não significa aumento imediato de preços no Brasil.

Parte da produção pode voltar para o mercado brasileiro

Se um produto deixar de ser exportado para os EUA, a empresa pode tentar vendê-lo no mercado doméstico. Se houver aumento relevante da oferta, isso pode pressionar os preços para baixo.

Empresas podem reduzir produção e emprego

Quando não há mercado alternativo, a saída pode ser reduzir a produção, adiar investimentos, suspender contratações ou cortar postos de trabalho.

Uma piora das perspectivas para o comércio exterior pode aumentar a percepção de risco e pressionar o real. Um dólar mais caro encarece produtos e insumos importados e pode dificultar a queda da inflação.

É nesse último ponto que o tarifaço pode chegar de maneira mais ampla à economia brasileira.

Para André Matos, CEO da MA7 Capital, o impacto do tarifaço sobre a economia brasileira é principalmente setorial e concentrado em determinadas regiões, e não deve representar um choque de grande proporção sobre o PIB.

Segundo o MDIC, os EUA representaram 10,8% das exportações brasileiras em 2025. No acumulado de janeiro a agosto de 2026, a participação caiu para 9,6%.

Por isso, uma queda nas vendas para o mercado americano pode atingir de forma significativa empresas e trabalhadores ligados à exportação, mesmo que o efeito sobre a economia como um todo seja limitado.

Segundo Matos, o impacto também depende da capacidade de redirecionar as exportações para outros mercados. Parte das vendas que deixaram de ir para os EUA foi absorvida por outros destinos, especialmente na Ásia.

Para o economista, porém, os juros elevados representam hoje um obstáculo mais abrangente para a atividade econômica: “Se eu tiver que ordenar os freios do crescimento, juro vem primeiro, com folga, e tarifa vem depois.”

O efeito da tarifa, segundo ele, também tende a ser mais lento. Uma empresa que perde um contrato com um comprador americano pode levar anos para recuperar esse mercado, mesmo que as condições comerciais melhorem.

Por que o consumidor não sente a tarifa imediatamente?

Para Matos, o impacto direto sobre os preços no Brasil tende a ser limitado porque a tarifa é cobrada na entrada dos EUA e paga pelo importador americano.

Além disso, produtos que deixam de ser enviados para os EUA podem ser redirecionados para outros mercados, inclusive o brasileiro. O aumento da oferta doméstica pode, em alguns casos, pressionar os preços para baixo.

“Para o consumidor, o efeito de curto prazo é neutro ou até levemente favorável. O problema dele não é preço, é emprego, se a empresa da região dele exportava para lá.”

Segundo Matos, o principal caminho para o tarifaço afetar os preços no Brasil seria indireto, pelo dólar . Se o aumento das tarifas elevar a percepção de risco sobre o Brasil, a moeda americana pode subir frente ao real.

Com o dólar mais caro, aumentam os custos de produtos e matérias-primas importados, como combustíveis e fertilizantes, o que pode pressionar a inflação.

Assim, o impacto tende a aparecer primeiro nas empresas que exportam, no emprego e nos investimentos. Só depois, dependendo do comportamento do dólar, pode chegar aos preços pagos pelos consumidores.

articles.title: 'O Menino da Porteira' faz 71 anos: como a música virou filme | G1
articles.standfirst: Gravada originalmente em 1955, canção ganhou projeção nacional na voz de Sérgio Reis, inspirou dois filmes e já teve 219 regravações.
articles.summary: Gravada originalmente em 1955, canção ganhou projeção nacional na voz de Sérgio Reis, inspirou dois filmes e já teve 219 regravações.
articles.body:
A música "O menino da porteira" completou 71 anos consagrada como uma das clássicas da cultura brasileira.

A canção composta por Ted Vieira e Luizinho virou ganhou monumento, virou filme e chegou até o Grammy Latino. Confira no vídeo acima.

Sua gravação original aconteceu em 1955. Em 1973 foi regravada por Sérgio Reis. Segundo o cantor, a ideia de regravar aconteceu após um, baile de debutante, em que a música fez sucesso.

"Que violeiro não canta 'O menino da porteira'? Onde você vai a turma canta junto", diz Sérgio Reis.

Até o momento, a música já foi regravada 219 vezes, segundo o Escritório Central de Arrecadação e Distribuição (Ecad).

Entre 1975 e 1976, a música virou filme e o cantor foi o protagonista. A ideia foi do cineasta Jeremias Moreira, como um protesto contra a ditadura militar. No longa, o vilão, o "Major", representa o regime. Sem sofrer censura, o filme fez sucesso e bateu recordes de bilheteria.

Em 2009, o longa ganhou uma nova versão. Dessa vez, o protagonista foi o cantor Daniel. As gravações ocorreram na fazenda do artista, que a disponibilizou para a equipe.

A trilha sonora do filme ganhou o Grammy Latino de 2009 na categoria "Álbum de música de raízes brasileira - regional nativa".

Em 2001, Ouro Fino construiu um monumento ao Menino da Porteira na entrada da cidade.

Hoje, a canção continua chegando a pessoas que nem eram nascidas quando ela foi gravada. Ouro Fino, por exemplo, mantém uma escola de música gratuita para quem quer aprender os sons da cultura caipira, onde ela é ensinada.

Saiba mais da história da canção nos vídeos abaixo.

articles.title: Elon Musk intensifies attack on Ambani over Starlink India launch delay
articles.summary: Elon Musk has accused Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani of blocking competition.
articles.body:
As SpaceX struggles to launch Starlink in India, Elon Musk has stepped up his attack on billionaire Mukesh Ambani, mockingly calling him the country's "prime minister" to suggest he wields outsized control over its government and accusing him of blocking the satellite internet service from competing.

On Friday, Musk continued his criticism of the famed Reliance Industries' chairperson in a post on X, arguing that Starlink could bring internet access to areas that remain unconnected, giving children more opportunities to learn, and helping small businesses reach customers worldwide.

"Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" Musk wrote.

Reliance Jio, Reliance Industries' telecom arm, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Musk's latest comments follow his accusations earlier this week that unnamed "oligarchs" were blocking Starlink's launch in India to protect their business interests. India's Ministry of Communications rejected the allegations, saying the country's regulatory framework for satellite communications is "fair and non-discriminatory." Musk then went further on Thursday, questioning Ambani's influence in a separate post on X. "Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he asked.

SpaceX has spent years trying to launch Starlink in India. Last year, it even struck distribution agreements with Ambani's Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel, India's second-largest telecom operator, to offer the service once it received the necessary approvals. However, Starlink has not yet received the go-ahead from New Delhi to begin commercial operations, despite securing key regulatory clearances .

In its Thursday statement, the Indian communication ministry said Starlink and two other licensed satellite operators are undergoing security assessments that must be completed before they can receive satellite spectrum. The ministry said all three are at "broadly the same regulatory stage," rejecting Musk's suggestion that Starlink was being singled out.

Jio and Airtel are also seeking to launch their satellite internet services in India. Jio has a joint venture with Luxembourg-based SES, while Airtel is a major shareholder in Eutelsat OneWeb, which is striving to offer satellite connectivity in the country.

India, the world's most populous country with over a billion internet users, is a major market for Musk. But expanding there also means dealing with powerful business figures such as Ambani, whose Reliance conglomerate owns India's largest telecom operator and works with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government on major projects.

articles.title: RBI takes steps to choke speculative bets against the rupee in forex market
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI said on Saturday it would sell dollars directly to IOC, HPCL and BPCL to meet their crude import needs, as part of measures to curb rupee
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI said on Saturday it would sell dollars directly to IOC, HPCL and BPCL to meet their crude import needs, as part of measures to curb rupee volatility. It also imposed a 20% cash reserve on banks for dollar purchases exceeding $2 million. Additionally banks must seek additional documentation of underlying exposure for extending rupee derivative contracts to clients.The tightened rules on forex derivatives aim to curb speculative positions, duplicate hedging and aggressive dollar buying. RBI’s weekend notification comes after India’s foreign exchange reserves fell by $51.1 billion from a record $785.71 billion in the week ended Sept 4 to $734.60 billion in the week ended Oct 2. The rupee has faced pressure from rising crude oil prices amid West Asian conflicts, foreign investor outflows from Indian equities and bonds, higher US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar amid global risk aversion. A big chunk of the reserve accretion, which followed the record mop up of $127 bn through FCNR(B) deposits.The measures bar traders from rebooking cancelled contracts, cut the limit for trading without proof of underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million, require undertakings against duplicate hedging.The targeted dollar-sale window is the first such facility for the three state-run oil marketing companies since Aug 2013, when RBI opened a forex swap window during the “taper tantrum” to meet their entire daily dollar needs. The companies then required around $8 billion to $8.5 billion a month for crude imports. Unlike the earlier arrangement, which involved RBI buying back dollars at a future date, the new facility involves direct sales.The intervention aims to divert predictable oil-import demand from the open market, where it can amplify pressure from corporate and portfolio outflows. India’s crude import bill fell to $121.8 billion in FY26 from $137.2 billion in FY25, according, despite crude imports rising marginally to 245.3 million tonnes. articles.title: Man did not file ITR, faced Rs 17.18 lakh penalty over alleged Rs 55.62 lakh unexplained cash deposits; ITAT Mumbai deletes penalty because tax officer invoked wrong provision
articles.summary: Unexplained cash can lead to a notice from the Income Tax Department, and sometimes even a penalty.
articles.body: Unexplained cash can lead to a notice from the Income Tax Department, and sometimes even a penalty. But what happens if the penalty is imposed under the wrong section?In one such case, the Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that a tax officer cannot impose a penalty under one provision of the Income Tax Act when the assessment order records that proceedings were being initiated under different provisions.What the case is aboutA man had not filed an income tax return for assessment year 2016-17. The tax department subsequently completed a reassessment without his participation and, on February 15, 2024, assessed his total income at Rs 55.62 lakh.The amount was treated as unexplained cash deposits in a bank account that the department attributed to him. The assessment order referred to Section 68 at one point and later treated the amount as unexplained money under Section 69. It also directed that tax be charged under Section 115BBE.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemptionAt the end of the assessment order, the officer recorded that penalty proceedings were being initiated under Sections 271AAC and 272A(1)(d).The tax department also imposed a penalty, but under Section 271(1)(c), which deals with concealment of income or furnishing inaccurate particulars of income. On August 21, 2024, the officer levied a penalty of Rs 17,18,658, calculated at 100% of the tax sought to be evaded.The man challenged the penalty, but the National Faceless Appeal Centre, Delhi, upheld it on January 23, 2026. He then approached the tribunal.Why he won relief from penalty in ITATHis objections went beyond the penalty. He argued that he was a non-resident and that the bank account did not belong to him. He also pointed out references in the assessment order to assessment year 2019-20 and financial year 2018-19, rather than the year under consideration.Those issues concern the underlying tax assessment, which the man has challenged separately. The tribunal did not decide them in this appeal. It focused on whether the officer could legally impose a penalty under Section 271(1)(c) when the assessment order had recorded the initiation of proceedings under other provisions.Also Read | Man opted for VRS after employer shut plant, got Rs 65.21 lakh and reported it as advance salary in ITR; Section 89 relief was denied, but ITAT Pune later ruled it a non-taxable capital receiptThe tribunal went back to the assessment order to establish exactly what the officer had recorded. Its finding was straightforward: the order mentioned Sections 271AAC and 272A(1)(d), but contained no corresponding direction to initiate penalty proceedings under Section 271(1)(c).That omission was central to the case. Section 271(1B) provides for deemed satisfaction in specified circumstances where an assessment order contains a direction to initiate penalty proceedings under Section 271(1)(c). The tribunal found that the necessary direction was missing here.The officer could not simply switch to a different penalty provision later, the tribunal held. Sections 271AAC and 271(1)(c) are distinct provisions, and initiating proceedings under one does not amount to initiating them under the other.There was also a problem with the penalty order itself. It stated that proceedings under Section 271(1)(c) had been initiated during the assessment. But the assessment order did not support that statement. The tribunal held that the later order could not make good the missing requirement or change what had been recorded earlier.Amit Gupta, Partner at Saraf and Partners says that the judgement emphasizes on the rule of the law with respect to distinction between penalty proceedings, vis-à-vis, underlying assessment proceedings.“It’s important to note that proceedings for imposition of penalty even though the same may emanate from assessment, are independent,” he tells TOI.According to Gupta, the judgement goes to highlight that the taxpayer can very well challenge the vires of the penalty proceedings independently and the merits/validity of the assessment or reassessment in pursuance of which penalty is levied can be challenged separately but cannot be the subject matter of penalty proceedings.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claimChapter XXI in the Income tax Act, 1961 enacts provisions for the levy, imposition and collection of penalty. It plays an integral role for the effective implementation of the tax statute and acts as an important deterrent for the evasion of tax by taxpayers.Section 271(1) makes appropriate provision to regulate levy of penalties on assessee in case of concealment of income or furnishing of inaccurate particulars of such income.“Accordingly, the existence of conditions stipulated in Section 271(1)(c) are a sine qua non for initiation of penalty proceedings under Section 271 and such existence should be clearly reflected in the underlying assessment order,” Gupta explains.“Furthermore, power to impose a penalty under section 271(1) hinges upon the satisfaction of the concerned officer in the course of assessment proceedings and it cannot be exercised if he is not satisfied and has not recorded his satisfaction about the existence of conditions,” he adds.Equally essential is the direction to initiate proceedings under Section 271(l)(c) which is pre-requisite for initiation of the penalty proceedings because of the deeming provision contained in Section 271(1B) of the ITA.In this backdrop, ITAT held the penalty initiation under Section 271(1)(c ) was without jurisdiction since the Assessing Officer had specifically initiated penalty proceedings under Section 271AAC (applicable to certain unexplained income taxable under Section 115BBE) and not under Section 271(1)(c) relating to concealment of income or furnishing inaccurate particulars.Also Read | Man paid Rs 1.73 crore for Gurgaon flat, waited over a decade without possession; builder alleges homebuyer bought it for commercial gain, consumer commission awards refund with 12% interest & Rs 4 lakh“Since the assessment order contained no satisfaction or direction for initiation of penalty under Section 271(1)(c), the subsequent levy under that provision was held to be invalid and an incurable jurisdictional defect since penalty provisions are distinct and cannot be interchanged. Initiation under Section 271AAC cannot be treated as initiation under Section 271(1)(c),” Gupta says.The tribunal explained that the validity of the penalty was a separate question from whether the Rs 55.62 lakh addition would ultimately stand. Even if the addition were upheld, the penalty could not survive without valid initiation under Section 271(1)(c).Nor did the tribunal see a reason to wait for the pending appeal over the addition. The tribunal therefore deleted the penalty of Rs 17,18,658.It’s important to note that the decision is limited to that penalty. It does not establish that the cash deposits were wrongly treated as income, or that the disputed bank account did not belong to the man. You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, sábado 10 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este sábado
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este sábado
articles.body: En este sábado, el precio de la electricidad se encarece notablemente en comparación con el día anterior, según datos del Operador del Mercado Ibérico de la Energía (OMIE). El precio medio de la electricidad en este sábado se sitúa en 130 €/MWh, lo que representa un aumento de 22,63 € respecto al día anterior, que cerró en 107,37 €/MWh. Este incremento llama la atención en un día de consumo habitual. A continuación, se analizarán las horas más caras y más baratas de este día para optimizar el gasto energético. Los precios de la electricidad se concentran en bloques horarios específicos, alcanzando su pico entre las 20:00 y las 22:00. Durante este intervalo, los costos se disparan, destacando 218.87 €/MWh a las 20:00 y 215.3 €/MWh a las 21:00, lo que indica que las horas más caras son segmentadas pero se mantienen elevadas por varios tramos. Además, aunque hay un leve repunte en la franja de las 18:00 a las 19:00 con 137.19 €/MWh, la mayor parte de los precios altos está recopilada en estas horas centrales de la noche. La luz es más barata en las franjas horarias nocturnas y durante las horas centrales del día. Las mejores oportunidades de ahorro se concentran principalmente entre las 11:00 - 12:00, 12:00 - 13:00, 13:00 - 14:00 y 14:00 - 15:00, donde los precios alcanzan valores mínimos de hasta 0.03 €/MWh. En este rango, se puede observar una ventana amplia de precios bajos, permitiendo un ahorro considerable si se ajustan los patrones de consumo. El análisis de las franjas horarias revela una notable diferencia de precios a lo largo del día, con un range que oscila desde un sorprendente mínimo de 0,03 €/MWh en la franja de las 12:00 a 13:00 hasta un máximo de 218,87 €/MWh en la franja de las 20:00 a 21:00. Esta gran amplitud en las variaciones de precios resalta la importancia de la planificación del consumo eléctrico por parte de los usuarios, ya que optimizar el uso de la energía en base a estos valores puede llevar a ahorros significativos.

articles.title: Government to announce a policy on stockpiling of critical minerals
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Recognising the importance of critical minerals for economic growth, green energy transition and national security, Government is set to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Recognising the importance of critical minerals for economic growth, green energy transition and national security, Government is set to announce a new policy on stockpiling these resources to ensure supplies to strategic sectors such as defence, aerospace and energy.Mines secretary Keshav Chandra said Friday that the policy was being finalised and was likely to be unveiled in a month. Talking to reporters on the sidelines of India Mines and Minerals Conclave 2026, organised by industry body Assocham, Chandra said govt was also working on four dedicated critical minerals processing parks in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Gujarat and Maharashtra to process raw materials brought from overseas.Critical minerals such as copper, lithium, nickel, cobalt and rare earth elements are essential for clean energy technologies and are increasingly used in wind turbines, electricity networks, electric vehicles and battery manufacturing.Addressing the conference, Chandra also emphasised the need to accelerate exploration, strengthen critical mineral capabilities, promote recycling and beneficiation, and adopt modern mining practices.“We have to look at innovative methods to make use of that wealth of information. Any country which has made spectacular progress is also utilising its wealth and infusing new technology, looking at the entire resource from a new perspective altogether,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Amid reports of shortages, govt says coal stocks improving at power plants
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid reports of shortages of dry fuel at thermal power plants, govt on Friday said the daily supplies of coal to the power sector have
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid reports of shortages of dry fuel at thermal power plants, govt on Friday said the daily supplies of coal to the power sector have increased by around 36% from Sept and the rate of stock depletion has moderated significantly.The coal ministry in a statement said that the tag ‘critical stock’ was just an early warning sign and didn’t mean that the plant was running out of the dry fuel. It added that plants showing low stocks were being closely monitored and the supplies were being redistributed to ensure uninterrupted power generation.“The ‘critical stock’ tag is a norm-based trigger (plants holding less than the prescribed threshold of normative stock) and is designed to flag plants early, well before actual fuel shortage or generation loss occurs. A plant appearing on this list is, by design, an early-warning entry and not an indication that it has run out of coal or is at imminent risk of shutting down,” the ministry said in a statement.As per the Central Electricity Authority, 87 of 190 coal-fired power plants had critical stocks as on Oct 8, up from 50 in the first week of Sep. The plants had 20.6 million tonne of coal, just 33% of the recommended stock of 61.2 million tonne.The ministry said that daily coal supplies to the power sector had risen by around 36% from the Sep low, with Oct averaging about 9% higher than the last month and the rate of stock depletion had also moderated significantly. “Stock depletion has slowed sharply, with the daily drawdown falling by more than half from 0.243 MT/day in Sept to 0.116 MT/day in Oct. The position is therefore stabilising, although stock rebuilding is yet to commence,” the ministry said, adding that rail loading had also strengthened correspondingly, averaging over 465 rakes per day in Oct, with the 470-rake target achieved on three consecutive days. Supplies through other modes, including road, have also improved, it added.With monsoon receding, the ministry said that peak power demand was expected to moderate by mid-Oct and sustained loading of 465-475 rakes per day should support further stabilisation and enable stock rebuilding ahead of the festive, winter and subsequent summer demand periods. This will help in reducing the number of plants in the critical category, coal ministry said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Transmission delays behind RE curtailment, not excess capacity: MNRE secy
articles.summary: New Delhi: Rejecting concerns that India was adding renewable energy capacity beyond what the power system can absorb, new and renewable energy secretary
articles.body: New Delhi: Rejecting concerns that India was adding renewable energy capacity beyond what the power system can absorb, new and renewable energy secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi said delays in transmission infrastructure were primarily responsible for curtailment of renewable power.Talking to TOI, Sarangi said renewable capacity is generally developed against identified demand - through power purchase agreements, contracts with commercial and industrial consumers, or distributed renewable energy schemes such as PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar. Curtailment has largely resulted from delays in transmission lines needed to evacuate renewable power. In some cases, projects are using temporary general network access, but the additional transmission capacity available under such arrangements cannot be assured round the clock.“So, from that point of view, you can’t claim that we have more RE capacity than is needed,” Sarangi said. “The solution is to expedite the transmission lines and complete them, and the second is to use more and more battery energy storage.”Curtailment of renewable energy - the intentional reduction or restriction of electricity output from sources such as wind or solar when generation exceeds the grid’s transmission capacity or local demand - has emerged as a major challenge for developers as well as the govt. In the first quarter of the ongoing financial year, nearly 8,133 gigawatt-hours of solar power was curtailed, which is estimated to be equivalent to 1.5 days of the country’s total electricity consumption.Sarangi said battery storage could also help improve utilisation of transmission infrastructure in renewable energy-rich regions. Solar-heavy transmission lines are typically used for only six to eight hours during the day. If sufficient battery storage is available, the same transmission network can be used to evacuate stored power during night hours.This could increase transmission capacity utilisation and allow more renewable energy to be connected to the same substations. Sarangi said the ability to expand and utilise renewable energy along with battery energy storage has much greater potential, with transmission utilisation potentially increasing almost two-fold in some solar-dominated areas.According to a Rubix Data Sciences report, India needs over 236 GWh of battery energy storage systems by FY 2031-32 to enable seamless integration of the increasing share of renewable energy into the grid. The cumulative installed BESS capacity currently stands at about 13.5 GWh, with over 150 GWh in the pipeline.Sarangi said both co-located and standalone BESS projects would be required. While co-located storage would be preferable for renewable energy projects as it would improve utilisation of transmission lines, standalone systems would be useful for managing surplus power and peak demand.On nearly 45GW of renewable energy projects that have received connectivity but are unable to sign power purchase agreements, Sarangi said a proposed amendment by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission could provide an exit route for developers, allowing them to surrender connectivity without losing the bank guarantee furnished for it.You use AI every day. articles.title: Love over lavishness: Indriya turns Diwali into a festival of love with Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth
articles.summary: Every festive season, from Dhanteras and Diwali to the weddings that follow, Indians buy gold as much for tradition and sentiment as for style.
articles.body: Every festive season, from Dhanteras and Diwali to the weddings that follow, Indians buy gold as much for tradition and sentiment as for style. And year after year, jewellery campaigns try to outdo each other with grand celebrations, sweeping visuals and big family gatherings.This year, Indriya, Aditya Birla Jewellery, has chosen a different route. Its festive campaign, Festival of Love, featuring Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth, sets aside the spectacle to focus on something far more familiar. The small gestures of affection that unfold between people in the middle of all the preparation.Most households will recognise the premise. Festivals bring homes alive with decorations, rituals, gifts and guests. Yet, amid the bustle, it is the simplest moments of connection that stay with us longest. For Indriya, which is steadily expanding its presence across the country, the festive season is also a chance to build a deeper bond with consumers at a time when emotion and purchase decisions go hand in hand.Sandeep Kohli, CEO, Indriya, said, “The festive season remains one of the most important periods for the jewellery industry, shaped by the enduring traditions of celebration, gifting and auspicious purchases. As Indriya continues to expand its presence across India, we see this as an opportunity to build deeper emotional connections with consumers through stories that resonate with how they celebrate today. With ‘Festival of Love’, we wanted to spotlight the relationships and moments that make the festive season meaningful, while Padmika brings this sentiment to life through jewellery inspired by prosperity, blessings and new beginnings. Together, they reflect our vision of creating jewellery that is rooted in Indian culture yet relevant for the modern consumer.”A Diwali story, told in the little momentsThe campaign film follows Aditi and Siddharth as they prepare to host friends for Diwali. There is no dramatic arc. Instead, the story moves through the familiar bustle of festive preparations, punctuated by playful banter, thoughtful gestures and the easy companionship of two people entirely at home with each other. Much of the film’s charm rests on the couple’s natural chemistry, which lends it a warmth that feels lived-in rather than staged.The emotional high point arrives as the evening unfolds. A thoughtful gesture becomes the centre of attention, prompting their friends to teasingly ask, “Aaj Diwali hai ya Valentine’s Day? (Is today Diwali or Valentine’s Day?)” The line lands lightly, with humour rather than sentimentality, and that is precisely its strength. In a single moment, it captures the campaign’s central idea: that love rarely announces itself, and often finds expression in the simplest, most unexpected ways.Shantiswarup Panda, Head of Marketing and Visual Merchandising, Indriya, said the intent was to look inward rather than outward. “This festive season, we wanted to move beyond the larger spectacle of celebration and focus on the moments of affection and connection that often unfold quietly within it. Aditi and Siddharth brought this thought to life effortlessly. As a couple, they embody the warmth, playfulness and genuine companionship that the campaign seeks to celebrate, making the story feel authentic and relatable.”Padmika: Heritage craft through a contemporary lenThe jewellery at the heart of the story is Padmika, Indriya’s new festive collection crafted in 22KT gold and inspired by symbols of auspiciousness. Worn by Aditi throughout the film, the collection is woven into the narrative rather than simply placed alongside it.Its defining feature is the revival of Gulabi Meenakari, a traditional pink enamel craft, enriched here with delicate blue meenakari accents. These are paired with motifs such as Goddess Lakshmi and the lotus, enduring symbols of prosperity, abundance and new beginnings. The result reinterprets familiar festive symbolism through a modern design sensibility, with necklaces, earrings, bangles and statement pieces meant to be worn through the festive season and well beyond it.Beyond the sparkleIn a category where festive storytelling often leans on opulence, Festival of Love makes a quiet case for restraint. By pairing a relatable narrative with a collection that honours heritage craftsmanship, Indriya positions jewellery not merely as adornment but as part of the moments and relationships that give a celebration its meaning. It is a thought worth carrying into the season: long after the diyas are put away, it is the quieter glow of love that people remember.Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Novel Jewels by Times Internet’s Spotlight team.You use AI every day. articles.title: The case for hardware in the AI era is getting more compelling
articles.summary: Apple's trust, AI costs, and new AI versions of old devices (laptops and phones) are making a new case for hardware in the AI era.
articles.body:
The term now seems almost quaint, the "iPhone killer."

For almost two decades, tech companies have attempted to dethrone the king of gadgets without success. The phone market has since matured, and consumers have their pick that's been so "good enough" that Apple ( AAPL ) struggles to convince people to upgrade.

What's urgently driving the tech world now isn't an effort to directly subvert the smartphone but to find novel ways to package AI into old and new hardware.

And the case for doing it is becoming more persuasive.

Apple itself is getting in on the action. As with its lock on apps and services, Cupertino acts as an innovative landlord, extracting rents. And, as Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives put it , the company is looking to extend that strategy as "the toll collector on the consumer AI highway."

"Much of the debate has centered on whether Apple arrived early or late to generative AI," he wrote in a note earlier this week. "We think the question that matters more is how well the company can put useful AI in front of an installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices and 1.5 billion iPhones."

For any AI-infused device, trust will be key. And that's where Apple shines . While the new generation of AI labs wrestles with muddy debates about safety, mass unemployment, security vulnerabilities, and misuse, Apple has quietly gone about its business, burnishing its reputation.

No rogue AI agents or apocalyptic AI takeovers here. Just an upgraded Siri that everyone has been waiting for, and more ways to use apps that you already rely upon to get things done.

In a roundabout way, new AI-powered hardware might be the catalyst to weaken the dominance of the smartphone as the be-all and end-all consumer form factor.

Microsoft this week unveiled its Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra , designed to let users run AI models at home without relying on the cloud. That's another pathway for AI hardware to succeed. The idea of running your own micro-data center at home might not be for everyone, but it has a certain appeal when you look at how much AI can cost on the cloud.

Rather than use an online AI service, you can instead load an app on your computer, download the model of your choice , and get busy — essentially for the cost of your computer and power bill. For consumers and professionals whose main concern is maintaining privacy in the AI era, running a capable machine of your own has special appeal.

But perhaps Apple will join Microsoft in doing this, and maybe the iPhone will still be the point guard for a person's DIY AI model at home.

articles.title: Woman buys Rs 1.03 crore 3BHK in Bengaluru, but builder fails to provide specially-enabled parking; Karnataka RERA orders provision within 60 days and audited maintenance accounts
articles.summary: You buy an apartment with the builder promising some special parking provisions.
articles.body: You buy an apartment with the builder promising some special parking provisions. But the builder fails to deliver and collects steep maintenance charges from residents. What do you do?In one such case, a woman and her family bought a 3BHK ( 3 Bedrooms, Hall, Kitchen) from a builder in Bengaluru for Rs 1.03 crore. The builder promised two specially enabled parking spaces, and it was supposedly one of the property's key attractions.What the case is aboutThe builder's brochure and terms clearly referred to these parking facilities. However, he failed to deliver on that commitment.However, the problems did not end there. Although the family executed the sale deed in August 2024, the builder has still not formed an apartment association.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing partiesNot only that, he has allegedly been collecting steep maintenance charges from residents without offering a proper explanation or producing audited accounts to justify the amounts.Frustrated by the builder's conduct, the woman approached the Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) to seek legal action.On September 7, 2026, the Karnataka RERA tribunal ruled in her favour and also strongly criticised the builder for undermining homebuyers' expectations.Also Read | She worked as a teacher till 62 years of age instead of retiring at 60, but was denied gratuity because of extended service; Allahabad HC orders payment with 6% interestWhy did the homebuyer win the case?Subrata Mukherjee, Partner at SNG & Partners, Advocates & Solicitors, told ET that the homebuyer succeeded because Karnataka-RERA concluded that the builder was obligated to provide a separate car parking space for a physically challenged person.This took into account the specific regulatory requirements governing the project and the evidence submitted before the Authority.The homebuyers purchased the apartment under a Sale Deed dated August 6, 2024, for a total consideration of Rs 1,03,28,979.In December 2023, the builder sent an email to the homebuyer, assuring her that a specially enabled parking space would be provided. However, the promised facility was not made available.The woman then wrote to the builder, reminding about the applicable guidelines requiring the provision of specially enabled parking.She relied on the environmental clearance issued by the Karnataka government. Clause 32 of the clearance specifies that facilities such as ramps and separate parking spaces must be provided for physically challenged persons.Considering these exchanges alongside the specific conditions in the project's Environmental Clearance, the Authority concluded that the builder was obligated to provide the required facility.After examining this provision, the Karnataka RERA tribunal observed that the guidelines clearly required the builder to make arrangements for facilities, including ramps and dedicated parking spaces, for persons with disabilities.RERA said: “Hence, viewed from any angle, the respondent (builder) is bound to provide separate car parking for physically challenged.”On this basis, the tribunal directed the builder to provide parking spaces for specially enabled persons in the housing project within 60 days from the date of the order.Karnataka-RERA also held that the builder was required to establish an association of allottees in accordance with the applicable law once the project had been completed in all respects and the occupancy certificate or completion certificate had been obtained.Following the formation of the association, the builder would have to execute the deed of declaration and provide audited accounts along with details of the maintenance charges.Accordingly, the tribunal directed the builder to furnish audited accounts and revised maintenance charges while executing the Deed of Declaration. This was to be done after the project was fully completed, the Occupancy Certificate or Completion Certificate was obtained, and an Association of Allottees was formed in accordance with the law in force.Also Read | Housing society wanted to label Mumbai doctor a defaulter over Rs 1.42 lakh maintenance dues and 18% interest; why Maharashtra court has granted him interim protectionYou use AI every day. articles.title: 'Not the time to be skittish': Why Wall Street sees stocks rising by year-end
articles.summary: Wall Street still sees more gains for stocks heading into the end of the year.
articles.body:
Between strong, AI-driven earnings and favorable historical trends in midterm election years, Wall Street strategists see tailwinds for stocks heading into year-end, even as bond yields hang near 24-year highs .

"The path of least resistance into year-end is higher," Truist chief investment officer Keith Lerner said.

Wall Street expects S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) earnings to jump 30% year over year, with major banks set to kick off what could be a blockbuster quarterly reporting season .

Bubbling worries over the AI trade, including the risk of a slower pace or spending, have weighed on tech valuations. The Technology sector ( XLK ) now trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of around 21, down from roughly 35 at this time last year, Lerner noted.

"You also have this reset in the market and valuations, and sentiment that also suggests that we could see some upside before year-end," he said.

History is also on the side of a rally as the midterms approach. The fourth quarter has been positive for the S&P 500 about 84% of the time during midterm election years, and the average gain is about 7%

"The one outlier was 2018, and that should raise a little bit of a flag because that's when the Fed was also raising rates, or there was concern they were going to be too tight," Lerner said.

That doesn't mean strategists aren't factoring the impact of high rates into their year-end forecasts.

Last month, Yardeni Research lowered its year-end S&P 500 price target to 7,900 , citing rising bond yields. The revised target implies just over 1% upside from current levels.

Wall Street now expects the Fed to hold rates steady at its October meeting, after voting unanimously on a quarter-point hike in September.

Meanwhile, stocks have been jittery in recent sessions, and the breadth of the rally has narrowed .

On Friday, stocks recovered from a drawdown after a Bloomberg report that OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) expects to reach or exceed $70 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year, helping quell worries that the AI boom was running out of steam.

"Things are accelerating. So to me, these are buying opportunities, not the time to be skittish," Dan Ives, Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director, told Yahoo Finance last week.

"We're in the third inning of the AI revolution," he added.

UBS analysts also pointed to growing AI demand in their recommendations for investors, but suggested approaching it through a diversified portfolio.

"We recommend a diversified approach to tech, favoring high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries of AI spending, megacap platforms, and defensive tech firms," UBS chief investment officer of the Americas Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi said.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: 'Let's go to the mall': Why malls in America are cool again
articles.summary: Malls in America are back in style.
articles.body:
"For about 20 years, [going to the mall] was the thing," Naveen Jaggi, president of retail advisory services at commercial real estate firm JLL ( JLL ), told Yahoo Finance's Brooke DiPalma (video above). "So you think back to the '80s, right? So 'Fast Times at Ridgemont High' and movies like that talked about malls. Then malls kind of went on the down slope."

Now, he said, "the 13-, the 14-, the 15-year-old kid, mall's a cool place to go: 'Let's go to the mall."'

A key aspect of the comeback is subtraction: The US has "demolished around 500 or 600 malls over the last 10 years," Jaggi said, going "from 1,500 malls to roughly 950 malls."

"So when you get rid of the bad malls, what do you have left? The good stuff," he said.

The survivors got expensive makeovers. Operators such as Macerich ( MAC ) and Simon Property Group ( SPG ) spent "billions of dollars making their malls attractive," Jaggi said, turning them into places to "shop, eat, entertain, movies. You can do it all in one stop."

Food is a big part of the pitch. "We don't see food courts anymore," Jaggi said. "Now we see actual curated food options," from a Cheesecake Factory ( CAKE ) to an Eataly.

Given that the average US household eats out four times a week, Jaggi noted, if malls give "people options for eating out, they will eat out, and they'll stay longer."

articles.title: Can a lipstick tell you how the economy is doing? Why the answer isn't so simple
articles.summary: The economy or a recession may be the last thing on your mind when you buy lipstick but that little swipe of colour could have a bigger economic story to
articles.body: The economy or a recession may be the last thing on your mind when you buy lipstick but that little swipe of colour could have a bigger economic story to tell.Introduced nearly 25 years ago, the Lipstick Index suggests that our beauty buys may reveal more about the ongoing financial circumstances than we realise. The theory is simple: when money gets tight, consumers may put big-ticket purchases such as holidays and designer handbags on hold, but still make room for smaller indulgences such as lipstick, perfume and cosmetics. After all, a little luxury may feel more affordable when the bigger splurges have to wait.After all, a little retail therapy can lift the mood without leaving a luxury-sized hole in the wallet. But does this feel-good fix still hold up when money gets tight?India’s beauty market certainly adds colour to the debate. In 2025, consumers bought a whopping 1,750 lipsticks every hour, through beauty retail website Nykaa. That’s a lot of pouts, but does it mean shoppers are reaching for a fresh shade when their budgets are under pressure?A small survey suggests otherwise. More than half the respondents said they had never bought lipstick as a little treat during financially difficult times.So, does the Lipstick Index still have a place in India, or is the theory beginning to smudge?Why lipstick became an economic indicatorThe Lipstick Index or the lipstick effect, in general, is built on the idea that when budgets get squeezed, consumers may put expensive purchases on pause but keep smaller luxuries in play.Leonard Lauder, then chairman of Estée Lauder, popularised the term in 2001 after observing a rise in lipstick sales during a US economic slowdown. The logic was that a holiday or designer handbag may feel like a stretch for buyers, but a new lipstick can still offer a little indulgence without a luxury-sized bill.The idea of affordable luxury, however, is older than the term itself. After World War II, fashion houses such as Chanel, Dior, Yves Saint Laurent and Balenciaga offered consumers a more accessible taste of luxury through perfumes and cosmetics, rather than expensive designer clothing.Explaining the consumer psychology behind the index, Jeff Kreisler, head of behavioural science at JP Morgan Private Bank, said that consumers may find it easier to absorb a price increase on an inexpensive item than on something as costly as a house.When bigger financial goals feel out of reach, smaller treats can offer a little comfort without putting the same pressure on the pocket.But before we declare lipstick the economy’s mood ring, there is a catch: a rise in sales does not automatically signal financial stress.Jyoti Prakash Gadia, managing director of Resurgent India, cautioned against applying the theory universally. “Just because there is an observation in one company or even broader category, it doesn't mean that this economic hypothesis is universally applicable,” he told TOI.India's beauty boom tells a different storyLipstick Index offers a useful lens on consumer behaviour, but is no crystal ball for predicting a recession in India.According to Gadia, “The Lipstick Index is a plausible and valuable hypothesis regarding consumer behaviour but cannot be regarded as an accurate predictor of recession in India.”He explained that smaller luxuries can offer a sense of satisfaction and normality during financially uncertain times without requiring a large outlay.“If one is in a relative financial distress, the individual may opt to make the gratifying indulgence smaller instead of altogether cutting out the indulgences. Lipsticks, perfume miniatures, and luxury snacks offer satisfaction, self-assurance and a feeling of normal stability, while requiring only small initial expenditure or investment,” he said.In short, consumers may choose smaller treats instead of giving up luxuries altogether. But whether lipstick makes the cut depends on individual budgets, priorities and spending habits. And when it comes to India’s growing beauty market, there is more than one shade to the story.From an economic perspective, this involves a cautious substitution; that is, buying something less costly, like a lipstick or a luxurious gourmet snack in place of a vacation, designer clothes or a more luxurious purchase. The consumer may be trying to hold onto some of the choices available to him or her amid uncertainty and financial tightening. Nonetheless, it all ultimately boils down to how much money the individual has.Rising lipstick sales may appear to support the theory, but the beauty boom has other possible drivers, too. Online shopping, wider product choices and premiumisation, when consumers move towards more expensive products within a category, can all influence spending.Furthermore, a growing beauty market, therefore, does not automatically mean shoppers are feeling financially squeezed.Online beauty seller Nykaa’s performance offers a glimpse of the sector’s growth. Its gross merchandise value (GMV) rose 28% year on year to Rs 4,105 crore in the first quarter of FY2027. Its House of Nykaa portfolio of owned brands recorded annualised GMV of around Rs 3,760 crore, up 39%.HUL’s Beauty and Wellbeing business reported a segment margin of 27.6% in the same quarter. However, its Home Care business grew faster, showing that the company’s growth was not confined to beauty products.Prices add another layer to the picture.In July 2026, personal care inflation stood at 2.24%, below headline inflation of 4.45%. By comparison, inflation in other personal effects, mainly jewellery and watches, reached 43.54%.With jewellery and watches becoming more expensive, beauty products might seem like a more affordable indulgence for some consumers.But buying lipstick because it fits the budget is not necessarily the same as buying it for comfort during financial stress. Nor do industry sales figures reveal whether shoppers are choosing lipstick instead of costlier purchases or simply spending more across categories.We asked 61 people. Here's what they saidA small TOI survey of 61 respondents explored lipstick-buying habits, spending preferences and go-to treats. While the findings offer a glimpse into consumer behaviour, the sample is too small to represent India's wider population.When budgets tighten, is lipstick still a treat?For most respondents, lipstick does not appear to be the first pick-me-up when budgets are stretched. More than half (51%) said they never bought lipstick as a treat during financially difficult periods, while another 25% said they rarely did so.Only 21% said they sometimes turned to a new lipstick for a little indulgence, and just 3% said they did so often. With around 76% rarely or never reaching for lipstick when money gets tight, the classic Lipstick Index does not quite hold up in this small survey.Lipstick also appears to be more of an occasional purchase than a regular mood-lifter. Around 55% of respondents said they bought it rarely or only when needed, while 22% purchased it every two to three months. Another 13% described their purchases as impulsive, while 5% bought lipstick whenever it was on sale and another 5% bought it every month. The findings suggest that for many, lipstick is more of a planned beauty purchase than an impulse buy or a go-to treat.Spending patterns point to a preference for the lower price brackets. Around 37% of respondents usually spent under Rs 500 on a lipstick, while an equal share spent Rs 500–1,000. Another 18% spent between Rs 1,000 and Rs 2,000, and 8% spent more than Rs 2,000. In all, nearly three-fourths spent up to Rs 1,000 per lipstick, suggesting that most respondents kept their purchases within this range.India has multiple income levels and segments and diverse tastes and hence, one product alone cannot be an indicator of the macro status of the economy. Financial planning requires us to consider affordable luxury expenses taking into account the overall consumer sentiments , inflationary trends, employment, and discretionary spending.Price or brand: What drives lipstick purchases?When it comes to spending, affordability appears to matter. Around 40% of respondents usually spent Rs 500–1,000 on lipstick, while 36% kept their spending below Rs 500.By comparison, 17% spent Rs 1,000–2,000, and 8% spent more than Rs 2,000. While spending habits varied, most purchases fell within the lower price brackets.Price, however, is not the only thing shaping buying decisions.Around 60% said both their budget and preferred brands influenced their choices. Another 17% prioritised the brand, while an equal share focused on the product and shade. Just 8% said budget was their main consideration.This suggests that even when shoppers are mindful of costs, the appeal of a particular brand, formula or shade can still influence what ends up in their beauty bags. The findings also show why affordability alone may not explain lipstick-buying habits: consumers can weigh price alongside their preferred products and brands.If not lipsticks, then what?If lipstick is not everyone's go-to pick-me-up, what else makes the list? Survey responses pointed to a range of alternatives, including food, clothes, skincare, other cosmetics, earrings, jewellery, face masks, trekking gear and plants. For some, even buying a favourite food item was enough to feel good.The choices underline how personal affordable indulgences can be. While one person might reach for a new lipstick, another might prefer a favourite meal, a skincare product or a pair of earrings. There is no single purchase that works as a mood-lifter for everyone.Gadia said the psychology behind the Lipstick Index could extend beyond cosmetics. Small purchases may offer gratification, self-assurance and a sense of normality when bigger financial goals seem distant. However, what counts as an affordable luxury can differ widely across income groups, regions and cultures in India.“There does not seem to be a common equivalent in India, since what constitutes an affordable indulgence differs by income group, geography and cultural traits,” Gadia said.He suggested that alternatives could include high-end tea or coffee, mithai, affordable artificial fashion jewellery, skincare samples and salon services.“For some consumers in urban areas, a visit to a cafe could be an alternative to an expensive night out. For others, a low-cost grooming expense could serve as a substitute for an expensive clothing line. The above are illustrative examples and do not constitute actual indicators of a possible or impending recession.”The survey, too, does not establish that consumers are replacing expensive purchases with smaller treats. Instead, it offers a glimpse into how varied their choices can be, and why lipstick alone may not be enough to tell us how consumers are feeling about their finances.So, does the Lipstick Index work in India?Ultimately, the Lipstick Index may say as much about personal choices as it does about the economy. For some, a new lipstick is a little treat; for others, it could be their favourite food, a skincare product or even a new plant for the balcony.This makes the theory difficult to apply to India, where spending habits and budgets vary widely. Rising lipstick sales do not necessarily mean consumers are worried about money, just as falling sales do not automatically point to financial stress. Beauty trends, brand preferences and changing spending power can also influence purchases.So, while the Lipstick Index offers an interesting way to look at consumer behaviour, lipstick sales alone cannot tell us whether the economy is under pressure.Finding the right shade may be tricky, but reading the economy takes more than a lipstick tally!You use AI every day.
